speaker_notes: The previous capture showed how switching is grouped into bursts to regulate the secondary supply. This view looks at the faster switching cycles during an active interval. The USB-C voltage was set to 20 volts and the electronic load to 4.7 amps. Yellow is the half-bridge switch node, which drives both the charge-pump and isolated resonant branches. Across the ten-microsecond window, about ten cycles are visible, giving a switching frequency close to one megahertz. The switch-node waveform alternates between its high and low levels on each cycle. Green is the secondary bulk voltage and blue is USB-C VBUS. Both output channels are AC-coupled, so their displayed positions should not be read as DC output levels. The capture shows the switching waveform at the carrier timescale. Gate timing is not shown, so the voltage at turn-on cannot be read from this view.
transition: Connector-voltage measurements then show how the supply delivered power across the USB-C settings.
